text: Setting clear goals is the foundation of any successful project. To ensure your team is moving in the right direction, use the SMART criteria: your goals should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," you could say "increase user sign-ups by 20% in three months." Once your main goal is set, break it down into smaller milestones. These are key checkpoints that help you track progress and stay motivated. Each milestone should lead to a tangible deliverable, such as a report or a working prototype. Finally, it is crucial to achieve stakeholder alignment. This means communicating your goals clearly to everyone involved, from team members to clients, so that all parties share the same vision and expectations from the start.
